results.key_change: T12 filing reorganized risk factors and added credit ratings table detail but same fundamental risk categories (distribution relationships, health reform, catastrophe exposure) with no material escalation.

Core TYSABRI/PML risks and product concentration risks unchanged; minor language updates on JCV antibody testing frequency and new pipeline filings reflect normal year-over-year progress, not deterioration.

Nearly identical risk factors with routine date/figure updates (debt $8.1B to $8.9B, market cap $25.5B to $26.9B); added minor language on space utilization changes due to technology but no new material risks.
Removed the CSC option risk (potential $650-750M forced purchase obligation) which was a significant contingent liability; added standard cyber security language but no new material threats.

Same retail competition, consumer spending, and macro risk factors with minor wording updates; added pension funding and pandemic supply-chain disruption language but these are boilerplate expansions, not new material problems.

Entry and T12 texts appear to be from different sections (entry is MD&A financials, T12 is product descriptions), making direct risk factor comparison unreliable; underlying business showed strong growth continuity.
Same core retail risk factors with minor additions around IT systems upgrade and data center move risks, reflecting normal operational evolution for a growing off-price retailer.

Debt increased from $18.4B to $23.1B and added international joint venture exposure (Japan, South Korea, Mexico, Malaysia, Klepierre stake), but these reflect growth-driven expansion rather than distress; core risk language unchanged.
Nearly identical cautionary language with minor additions on congressional spending/debt ceiling uncertainty and IP infrastructure transition; standard telecom regulatory risk updates.

Entry and T12 texts cover different portions of the filing (entry is environmental/emissions detail, T12 is regulatory overview), but both reflect standard utility regulatory and environmental compliance risks with no material escalation.
Both filings contain only the risk factor table of contents with identical risk categories; page numbers shifted by one page but no content changes detectable.

Entry text is MD&A (not risk factors) while T12 is actual Item 1A risk factors, making direct comparison unreliable; T12 risk factors appear to be standard software company disclosures around competition, security, and tax regulation.

T12 discloses First Niagara acquisition with S&P and Fitch changing outlook to negative, adds elevated CRE valuation and oversupply concerns, and new integration risk -- representing material new risks beyond entry profile.

Removed management transition risk (new team now established), noted Congress passed five-year infrastructure funding bill and eleven states increased transportation funding, reducing key demand uncertainty.

Added substantial SanDisk integration risks (costs, culture, internal controls), goodwill impairment warning due to market cap volatility, and Brexit macro risk; MOFCOM restrictions partially resolved but replaced by complex merger execution risk.
